newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on exports, S. America.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on exports, S. America.

text.p: A slowdown in the U.S. export sales pace and rainfall over the weekend in key South American soybean growing regions pressed CBOT soybean futures to a lower close, traders said.
"It opened lower on South American rains, tried to rally but then was pressured by a disappointing export number for soybeans," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

Traders again were reminded of the near-ideal crop weather in Brazil and Argentina and received further bearish input from USDA's weekly export inspections report. USDA cited soy inspections at only 20.495 million bu for the week ended Dec 5.
That tally was well below trade estimates for 28 to 33 million bushels and was sharply below the 35.321 million the previous week.
Traders said there was little other news to provide direction with Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report offering few surprises.
CFTC said as of December 3, funds were long soybeans roughly 117.8 million bushels and short by about 99.0 million.
Soybeans closed 3-1/2 to nine cents per bushel lower, with January down 7-1/4 at $6.88-3/4.
Traders also said news from the National Grain and Feed Association conference Monday in Kansas City was bearish for grains and soybean futures markets.

Sparks Companies CEO Carrol Brunthaver said large world supplies will weigh on U.S. soybean exports and prices next spring. Brunthaver said China had probably completed its soybean and soymeal purchases for the year and Brazil and Argentina were forecasting record soybean crops which would likely attract buying interest from Pacific Rim countries.
ADM Investor Services sold 3.5 million bushels of March, Refco Inc bought and sold two million bushels of January, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 42,000 contracts, above the 41,432 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, Refco Inc bought 300 March $7.25 calls and sold 300 March $6.75 calls at 18-3/4 cents.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, above the 8,818 traded Friday.
